stem: A nurse explains chronic kidney disease classification to a client. Which framework reflects current KDIGO CKD classification?

options.A: Cause, blood-pressure category, and serum sodium category
options.B: Cause, GFR category, and albuminuria category
options.C: Cause, serum sodium category, and body-mass-index category
options.D: Cause, hemoglobin category, and blood-pressure category

rationale: KDIGO 2024 classifies CKD using the CGA framework: Cause, GFR category (G1–G5), and Albuminuria category (A1–A3). Therefore B is correct. Blood pressure, sodium, body mass index and hemoglobin can be clinically relevant in CKD but are not the three components of the KDIGO CKD classification framework.
educational_objective: Recall the KDIGO CGA framework used to classify chronic kidney disease.
source_document_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source_version_date: April 2024; current CKD classification guideline as accessed 2026-08-16
source_locator: Definition and classification of CKD, printed p. S137: CKD is classified based on Cause, GFR category (G1–G5), and Albuminuria category (A1–A3), abbreviated CGA; Tables 2 and 3.
source_claim_supported: Current KDIGO CKD classification is Cause + GFR category + Albuminuria category (CGA).

source_original.source_detail: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Definition and classification of CKD, Kidney International 105(Suppl 4S), printed p. S137: CKD is classified based on Cause, GFR category (G1-G5), and Albuminuria category (A1-A3), abbreviated CGA; Tables 2 and 3 define the GFR and albuminuria categories. KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline remains the current global CKD guideline; focused Chapter 3 update is underway but has not superseded the classification section.
